title: Feasibility trial of a transdiagnostic psychotherapy to improve mental health, resilience and long-term stability: Well-Being Therapy (WBT) as a group intervention in a day-clinic overall treatment concept.
summary: Well-Being Therapy (WBT) according to Fava focuses psychotherapeutic work on positive feelings and achieving a balanced state of well-being instead of simply concentrating on minimizing suffering. With this change of perspective, WBT addresses an often neglected aspect of mental health (WHO). The pursuit of greater well-being can lead to very positive effects and a significant improvement in quality of life for people with mental illnesses, especially those with chronic courses or residual symptoms. Through self-observation and working on various dimensions of well-being, WBT promotes mental resources, stability and resilience and thus represents a useful addition and enrichment to the psychotherapy landscape. It combines proven behavioral therapy methods with a philosophical and growth-oriented basis, including flow experiences and lifestyle modifications. With its transdiagnostic approach, it seems particularly suitable for use in a general psychiatric day clinic. The present study aims to investigate the application of Well-Being Therapy as a group therapy intervention in a general psychiatric day clinic and to examine its acceptance, feasibility and effectiveness in this context.
conditions: Enduring personality changes, not attributable to brain damage and disease

interventions.name: Patients with different psychiatric diagnosis (affective disorders, psychotic disorders, anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive disorders, neurotic, stress or somatoform disorders, personality disorders) are recruited as part of their day clinic treatment. After completion of the 8-week day clinic

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants with sufficient knowledge of German. Patients must meet the diagnostic criteria for one of the following main diagnoses according to ICD10: diagnosis of an affective disorder (F30-F39), a psychotic disorder (F20-F29), an anxiety disorder (F40-F41), an obsessive-compulsive disorder (F42), a neurotic, stress or somatoform disorder (F43-F48) or a personality disorder (F60-F62) and participate in the program of the psychiatric day clinic, Clinic and Polyclinic for Psychiatry and Psychotherapy, University Hospital of Munich, LMU Munich.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients are excluded if they meet the ICD10 criteria for active substance dependence (abstinence for less than 6 months), an eating disorder, an organic mental disorder or acute suicidality (as a primary or comorbid diagnosis). Patients are screened and diagnosed by a trained clinician using the ICD10 criteria (mini-interview and SKID-5-PD). All patients are excluded who are currently pregnant or who suffer from an unstable or inadequately treated concomitant somatic disease including acute and chronic infections and autoimmune disease.
